ruleVersionReview.basis: The current FlatModifier adds2 to exactly ghost/dark/fairy damage-base selectors. The complete retained native Umbra page says: "Ghost, Dark, and Fairy-Type Attacks gain +2 DB." "The Light Level is treated as Darkness for all non-Ghost, Dark, and Fairy-Type creatures." Its affliction clause is: "When a Ghost, Dark, or Fairy-Type creature inflicts a Persistent or Volatile Status Affliction on a target, that target is also Cursed." Cursed is additional; the triggering Persistent or Volatile Status Affliction is retained, without replacement or removal. Its separate Hazard-creation clause is: "When used by a creature with the Ghost, Dark, or Fairy-Type, all Moves with the Hazard Keyword increase their Range by +2, and the number of Hazards they create is increased by 50% (minimum 1)." Range+2 concerns those Moves' Range; +50% (minimum1) concerns the number of Hazards they create, not arbitrary count-based effects. Its separate contact/affected-by-Hazard clause is: "When a creature comes into contact with or is affected by a Hazard created by Ghost, Dark, and Fairy-Type creature, that creature loses a Tick of Hit Points, in addition to the Hazard's normal effects." The literal "that creature" and "Ghost, Dark, and Fairy-Type creature" are retained without resolving referent or conjunction ambiguity beyond the source. Illumination implementation note: "In Foundry you can turn off Global Illumination to activate this, normal light sources such as Flashlights & the Glow Capability still function, and so would things like Darkvision." curse note: "This part of the effect is not Automated!" hazardCreation note: "This part of the effect is not Automated!" hazardContact note: "This part of the effect is not Automated!" All three clauses remain explicitly manual, not automated. Full weather Introduction describes a PTR overhaul proposal with unfinished distribution and tier priority/cancellation limits. Darkness has its own lighting-radius/accuracy/perception rules and local Actor UUIDs. A matching native +2DB clause is not independent approved authoring of this current weather effect, its lifecycle or omitted objects; unlimited expiry does not establish global application/removal. The unresolved source/version/use disposition remains.

fieldReview.recordValue: The user becomes Curled Up. While Curled Up, the user becomes immune to Critical Hits, and gains 10 Damage Reduction and +1 Defense Combat Stage. However, while Curled Up, the user is Slowed and their Accuracy is lowered by 4. The user may stop being Curled Up as a Rapid Action, or if they are Recalled or Take a Breather. If the user has Rollout or Ice Ball in their Move List, they do not become Slowed while Curled Up, and the user gains a +10 bonus to the damage rolls of those Moves and does not suffer Accuracy Penalties from being Curled Up when using those moves.
